## RYANAIR ANNOUNCES 1st ENGINE MRO TO SEVILLE


Following a competitive tender process, Ryanair, today (Tues, 17 Nov) announced that it has chosen Seville as the location for its first-ever engine repair, maintenance and overhaul (“MRO”) facility, representing a c.€500m investment and creating over 600 new highly skilled jobs in Andalusia.


The new 28,000 sqm facility at the Port of Seville will maintain, repair and overhaul Ryanair’s CFM56-7B and LEAP-1B engines, playing a critical role in Ryanair’s growth to 800 aircraft and 300m passengers by 2034. Construction will begin in early 2027, with the facility expected to open in 2029.


This will be Andalusia’s first-ever aircraft engine MRO facility, creating hundreds of highly skilled engineering jobs, further strengthening Seville’s position as a leading aerospace hub. Ryanair will also establish a new Engineering Academy in Seville to recruit and train the next generation of aircraft technicians and engineers, ensuring an ongoing stream of long-term training and employment opportunities across the region.


Following the selection of Seville as the first site for Ryanair’s two new engine MRO’s, a second MRO location will be confirmed in 2027. Together, these two engine MRO’s will be capable of carrying out c.400 full engine overhauls annually, supporting a fleet engine pool of up to 2,000 engines by 2034 and underpinning Ryanair’s growth to 800 aircraft and 300m passengers p.a. by FY34.

Ryanair, Europe’s No.1 airline, today (1st August) celebrated the first flight from Prague to Paphos, while on Monday (3rd August) it will launch a twice weekly service to Kosice, both as part of its extended Summer 2020 schedule.


To celebrate its new routes, Ryanair has launched a seat sale with fares from 729 Kc for travel to Kosice and from 759 Kc to Paphos, both until the end of October, which must be booked by Wednesday (5th August), only on the Ryanair.com website.
